chapter: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
title: The tunes she wrote for Decca, including Messa Stomp
summary: She lists the pieces: 'Froggy Bottom', 'Messa Stomp', 'A Lot of Sax Appeal', 'Mary's Idea' and 'Cloudy'. She did most arranging with Andy until Earl Thompson came in.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I did another thing on "Froggy Bottom" and I rearranged "Messa Stomp". That was my first arrangement. I think we recorded that once before when we recorded with Blanche, "Messa Stomp". That was my first composition. I got the title - my grandfather used to call me "Messy" and 'Messa', something like that, so I called it "Messa Stomp". Let's see, "Froggy Bottom" "Messa" 'Lotta', "A Lot of Sax Appeal" - oh, let's see, what else. Oh, there's 20 things. "Mary's Idea". "Cloudy". That was quite late.
This was all part of the first session for Decca?
Yes. We did all this in one week almost.
Up until then, before you sat down and wrote 20 things...right off the bat like that, about how much had you written for the band? Had you been writing for quite some time?

Yes, I guess I had given them almost a complete book because I was the only one writing at the time till Earl Thompson came in and then later on we picked up on other people, you know, on the outside. But I was doing most of the arranging, Andy and I.
